findings.headline: Rapid pace recovery after early wet‑to‑dry switch suggests earlier intermediate call
findings.detail: During the wet‑to‑dry transition (lap 19‑22) the medium tyres showed a +6.2 s delta then a -0.577 s improvement while stress stayed unrecorded; the huge delta indicates loss of grip, but the subsequent -0.577 s suggests the driver adapted quickly. Maintaining pace on the drying line avoided a larger time loss, so future strategy should consider an earlier switch to intermediates before lap 19.

findings.headline: Intermediate tyres gained grip as track dried, no extra pit required
findings.detail: From laps 27‑34 on intermediates the modelled degradation was -0.325 s/lap overall, yet lap 34 showed a -0.407 s improvement while track temp rose to 21.0 C. The driver extracted extra performance as the surface dried, indicating good tyre‑temperature management; no further tyre change was needed until lap 40.

findings.headline: Hard tyres hold pace under blue flags but show minor slip on lap 49
findings.detail: When the hard tyres were introduced on lap 40 (dry) the pace delta stayed at 0.0 s despite a blue flag on lap 41‑44, showing the driver could hold median pace under traffic. However lap 49 showed a +0.012 s delta with a blue flag, hinting a slight degradation when defending. Consider conserving a few seconds on lap 48‑49 to avoid losing position under blue.

findings.headline: Low end‑race stress implies mental fatigue was not a factor
findings.detail: Stress reading is missing for the critical wet‑to‑dry window (laps 19‑22), but the post‑race calm (16.4) and pre‑race tired (52.0) suggest the driver was not overly stressed during the race. With only two stress points the confidence is low; still, the low stress at the end indicates the driver finished relaxed, so mental fatigue likely did not affect final laps.

findings.headline: Soft tyres gave a clear pace boost on final laps
findings.detail: The soft tyre stint on laps 51‑52 delivered the fastest lap (88.293 s) with a -1.122 s delta on lap 52, but the stress value comes from post‑race radio, not in‑lap measurement. The performance gain is clear, yet we cannot confirm driver stress impact; still, the softs proved decisive for a final push.

findings.headline: Blue‑flag traffic had minimal impact on lap times
findings.detail: Blue flags appeared frequently from lap 21 onward, yet no pace delta spikes were recorded except a minor +0.012 on lap 49. With only a handful of blue‑flag laps, the data suggests the driver managed traffic without major time loss, but the sample is small.
